say: A Swiss fiduciary office. Three client files, in German, French and Italian, full of AHV numbers, IBANs, company IDs, birth dates and home addresses. Everything you see here is synthetic.
Treuhand Shield runs next to Apertus version 1.5, 8B, on llama.cpp, inside a Docker network with no route to the internet. The demo checks that first: both outside addresses are blocked.

Before anything reaches the model, the Swiss identifiers are found by their check digits, and Apertus itself, running locally, finds the names, companies and addresses. Each value becomes a reversible token. This is exactly what the model receives.
Apertus writes the task list on tokens only. The proxy puts the real values back before the employee sees the answer.
The demo searches every byte sent to the model for the twenty-six sensitive values. The audit log keeps counts and a hash chain, never values. Edit one event, and the chain breaks.

On thirty generated client notes, the local Apertus detector cuts the sensitive values that reach the model from forty-two percent to under two percent, and ninety-three percent of the requested values come back correct, against one hundred percent without protection.
One command, one machine, no cloud. Treuhand Shield with Apertus, open source under Apache 2.0.
